question.problem: The height of a cone is increasing at a rate of $24\,\text{ft}/\text{h}.$ The radius of the cone is always $\frac{3}{5}$ times its height. At what rate is the cone's volume increasing when its height is $6.25\,\text{ft}?$
question.worked_solution:
Let's call $h$ the height of the cone and $r$ the radius of its base. Both of these quantities, as well as the volume $v,$ change with time. In particular, we know that

$$
\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t}=24\,\text{ft}/\text{h},
$$

and we need to find $\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}$ when $h=6.25\,\text{ft}.$

We need to find a relation between $v$ and the variable for which we know the rate of change, which is $h.$ This is given by the formula for the volume of a cone:

$$
v=\frac{1}{3}\pi {r}^{2}h
$$

Before we differentiate the equation with respect to time, note that $r$ also appears in the formula. So, we need to simplify the formula by writing $r$ in terms of $h.$

We're told that the radius of the cone is $\frac{3}{5}$ times its height. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\frac{3}{5}h.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the volume formula as

$$
v=\frac{1}{3}\pi {(\frac{3}{5}h)}^{2}\cdot h=\frac{3}{25}\pi {h}^{3}.
$$

Now that we have an equation relating just $v$ and $h,$ we differentiate with respect to time using the chain rule. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}v & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{3}{25}\pi {h}^{3}) \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{9}{25}\pi {h}^{2}\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting the known values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{9}{25}\pi (6.25)^{2}(24) \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} & =337.5\pi \,{\text{ft}}^{3}/\text{h}.\end{aligned}
$$
